title: feat: shear (italic slant), vdenoise dctdnoiz/owdenoise, channel --mode base (RSI round 193)
body:
## Summary

RSI round 193 — three capabilities verified on ffmpeg 4.4 before shipping:

- `shear` — italic-style picture slant (`shear` filter): `--x`/`--y` shear factors -2..2, `--fill` edge color, `--interp nearest|bilinear`, `--at`/`--dur` windows via the shared split+blend path. Verified: `--x 0.6 --fill cyan` slants the frame with the vacated corner filled cyan.
- `vdenoise --engine dctdnoiz|owdenoise` — two more denoisers rounding out the engine set: DCT-domain (`sigma=s×5`, aggressive but edge-sharp) and overcomplete wavelet (`luma/chroma_strength=s×4`, smoothest result). Measured on a noise=25 flat fixture: luma stdev 16.1 → 2.5 (dctdnoiz) / 1.4 (owdenoise). Like bm3d, neither has timeline `enable` on 4.4 → `--at` returns a clear `input` error naming the windowed engines.
- `channel --mode base --pan -1..1` — `stereotools` stereo base: -1 folds an over-wide or phasey recording toward mono, +1 exaggerates width. Verified on a two-tone stereo fixture: L-R diff 2.5 → 5.2 at +1, → 0 at -1.

## Test plan

- [x] shear cyan fill measured in top-left corner (mean luma 178 vs input ~36)
- [x] shear `--at` window ok; dctdnoiz/owdenoise flat-stdev halved + `--at` rejected
- [x] channel base +1 widened / -1 folded to mono (L-R RMS diff)
- [x] `cargo test` 473 cli + 4 contract + 17 unit green; `clippy -D warnings` + `fmt` clean on ffmpeg 4.4 toolchain
